doc.title: Bruce Johnstone interviewed by Monk Rowe, Dunkirk, New York, October 11, 2013

title: Buddy Rich alumni, Jay Craig, and Onaje Allen Gumbs at Fredonia
summary: Rich school alumni like Menza and Ernie Watts; Jay Craig copied his licks; Rowe tells how student Onaje Gumbs was offered Rich's piano chair.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Um hum. Did that include Don Menza?
Yes. Menza, Pat LaBarbara, Bobby Shew, I mean, tons of them — Ernie Watts, all those guys came out of that school.
I guess if you can survive that then —

Yeah. He offered it to me I think three times and I turned him down three times because I was doing other stuff. But a guy who used to follow me around all the time, his name was Jay Craig, a Scottish baritone player who had gone to Berklee, and he used to dog my footsteps, no matter where I was. Copped all my licks. Got on Buddy’s band playing all my licks.

Do you know that there’s a little — now that you’re at Fredonia — there’s a little Fredonia story with Buddy. He came to play a concert, and this would have been probably ’72. And his piano player was either ill or whatever, they had no piano player that night. And Onaje Allen Gumbs —

Well, he was still a student here. And he played the whole concert with him. And Buddy Rich offered him the gig right on the bandstand, in the big hall, in King Hall. And of course all of us are going, “take it, take it!” I mean because that was our dream.
And here’s one of our own being asked. And he didn’t take it. I think he was smart. He was too gentle a soul. He could not have handled any of that. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -13-
Yeah. The Buddy Rich survivors are pretty tough guys. Personality-wise, they’re pretty bombastic.
